sections.text: Simulation is the answer when a system **resists closed form**: too many interacting random parts, non-Markovian dynamics, complex logic. You replace analysis with experiment — generate random inputs, run the system's rules, and estimate outputs statistically. The two pillars are **Monte Carlo** (estimate an integral/expectation by averaging random samples) and **discrete-event simulation** (advance a clock event-by-event through a system's state changes). The central trade-off: simulation gives answers when math can't, but at a **statistical** ($O(1/\sqrt{n})$) cost — variance reduction is how you buy back precision.
